newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly lower against the dollar on Tuesday in a quiet market, dealers said.
"The market was very quiet today and the shekel was stuck in a very narrow range," said a dealer at the First International Bank of Israel. "Volume was low and the market was trendless."
Just before the setting of the representative rate investors started converting shekels into dollars and the shekel fell to 3.5480 shekels per dollar, he said.
The dealer said there was no evident reason for the shekel's decline.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5440 shekels compared with 3.5410 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7645 against 3.7651 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded at 2.9913 per 100 yen compared with 2.9824 on Monday, and against the mark at 1.8851 shekels compared with 1.8916 on Monday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5500 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
